cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Scapula

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with the humeral head at the glenohumeral joint and with the clavicle at the acromioclavicular joint.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Spine, acromion, coracoid process, glenoid cavity, supraglenoid and infraglenoid tubercles, supraspinous/infraspinous fossae, subscapular fossa, borders and angles.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Rotator cuff muscles, deltoid, trapezius, biceps/triceps long heads, coracobrachialis, pectoralis minor, rhomboids, levator scapulae and teres muscles attach to the scapula.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Glenoid faces laterally; spine is posterior; subscapular fossa is anterior; inferior angle points down.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Acromion (of scapula)

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Scapula.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Deltoid arises from its lateral border and trapezius inserts on its medial/superior aspect; acromioclavicular and coraco-acromial ligaments attach nearby.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the summit of the shoulder and the roof over the glenohumeral joint/subacromial space.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Subacromial impingement may involve structures passing beneath the acromion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Spine of scapula

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Scapula.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Trapezius attaches to the superior lip and deltoid to the inferior lip.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Divides supraspinous and infraspinous fossae and expands laterally into the acromion.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Palpable posterior landmark useful for orienting the scapula.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coracoid process (of scapula)

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Scapula.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Short head of biceps and coracobrachialis arise from its tip; pectoralis minor inserts medially; coracoacromial, coracoclavicular and coracohumeral ligaments attach to it.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Projects anterolaterally above the glenoid and is palpable below the lateral clavicle.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Important landmark in shoulder surgery and in stabilisation of the acromioclavicular complex.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Clavicle

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates medially with the manubrium and laterally with the acromion.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Sternal end, acromial end, conoid tubercle, trapezoid line, subclavian groove and impression for costoclavicular ligament.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Pectoralis major, deltoid, trapezius, sternocleidomastoid and subclavius attach to the clavicle.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Sternal end is bulky; acromial end is flattened; conoid tubercle lies inferoposteriorly near the lateral end.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Humerus

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with the scapula proximally and with the radius and ulna distally.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Head, anatomical/surgical necks, greater/lesser tubercles, intertubercular sulcus, deltoid tuberosity, radial groove, condyles and epicondyles.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Rotator cuff inserts around the tubercles; pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi and teres major attach around the intertubercular sulcus.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Head faces medially, superiorly and slightly posteriorly; greater tubercle is lateral.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Glenohumeral ligament (thickening of joint capsule)

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Capsular thickenings extending from the glenoid/labrum region to the anatomical neck of the humerus.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Superior, middle and inferior glenohumeral ligaments.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Reinforces the anterior glenohumeral capsule and limits excessive translation depending on arm position.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: The inferior glenohumeral ligament complex is particularly important in resisting anterior dislocation.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coracohumeral ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the lateral base of the coracoid process to the greater and lesser tubercle region of the humerus, blending with the capsule.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Reinforces the superior glenohumeral capsule and helps resist inferior translation of the humeral head.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies superior to the glenohumeral joint and blends with rotator cuff/capsular fibres.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coraco-acromial ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the coracoid process to the acromion.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms the coracoacromial arch, limiting superior displacement of the humeral head.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the superior roof over the humeral head, subacromial bursa and supraspinatus tendon.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Can contribute to subacromial impingement.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Conoid part of coracoclavicular ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the base of the coracoid process to the conoid tubercle on the inferior clavicle.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Resists superior displacement of the clavicle and provides major vertical stability to the acromioclavicular joint.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: More medial and more vertically oriented than the trapezoid part.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Coracoclavicular ligament disruption is important in higher-grade acromioclavicular separations.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trapezoid part of coracoclavicular ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the superior surface of the coracoid process to the trapezoid line on the inferior clavicle.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stabilises the acromioclavicular joint and resists medial displacement/compression of the scapula relative to the clavicle.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: More lateral and more oblique/horizontal than the conoid part.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Subscapularis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Medially rotates and adducts the arm and stabilises the humeral head in the glenoid.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5–C7).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Subscapular fossa of scapula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lesser tubercle of humerus and anterior shoulder joint capsule.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Long head of biceps brachii

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Supinates the forearm and flexes the elbow; assists shoulder flexion and helps stabilise the humeral head.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Supraglenoid tubercle of scapula and adjacent superior glenoid labrum.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Tendon passes intra-articularly but extrasynovially across the humeral head and then through the intertubercular sulcus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Radial tuberosity and forearm fascia via the bicipital aponeurosis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Supraspinatus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Initiates the first ~15° of arm abduction and stabilises the humeral head in the glenoid.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Suprascapular nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Supraspinous fossa of scapula and overlying fascia.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Superior facet of greater tubercle of humerus and shoulder joint capsule.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Infraspinatus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Laterally rotates the arm and stabilises the humeral head in the glenoid.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Suprascapular nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Infraspinous fossa of scapula and overlying fascia.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Middle facet of greater tubercle of humerus and shoulder joint capsule.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Subacromial bursa

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Between the supraspinatus tendon/deltoid and the acromion-coracoacromial arch.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Reduces friction during movement of the rotator cuff and deltoid beneath the coracoacromial arch.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Closely related to the supraspinatus tendon and subdeltoid region; usually does not communicate with the glenohumeral joint.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Inflammation causes painful arc symptoms and may accompany rotator cuff impingement.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Subcoracoid bursa

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Lies beneath the coracoid process, between it and adjacent subscapularis/capsular structures.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Reduces friction between structures moving beneath the coracoid process.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Related to the subscapularis tendon and anterior shoulder capsule; may communicate variably with nearby bursae or joint recesses.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Can become inflamed and contribute to anterior shoulder pain.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Bursa between heads of teres major and latissimus dorsi

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Lies between the adjacent tendinous/muscular portions of teres major and latissimus dorsi near their humeral insertions.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Reduces friction between teres major and latissimus dorsi during shoulder movement.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Located near the medial and floor regions of the intertubercular sulcus where teres major and latissimus dorsi insert.
